match_note: Nature Communications file, transferred after two rounds at Nature Nanotechnology (those reports are not in the file). Three referees: R1, R2, and R3, an early-career co-reviewer of one report who made no comments of their own. Version 0 (round 1) matches arXiv v1 (12 Mar 2026). v1 has every feature the round-1 reports criticize: Eq. 1 written with geometric inductances only, with kinetic inductance mentioned and dropped in the text; the 3:1 areal asymmetry and the Is2>>Is1 single-arm extraction of LJ for the 45 degree device; Fig. 2(f) with the superfluid stiffness trace against bulk T^2 behavior; the phase-switching data in Extended Data Fig. 2 rather than Fig. 3; the sentence 'The role of the in-plane magnetic field ... is not well understood at this point'; the claim that the nominally 0 degree SQUID shows no zero-field diode effect and serves as a control; the 20 K phase data; and the flux-noise section. v1 has no 30 degree device and no D6 diode or histogram data, which the rebuttal adds. The cited line numbers (149, 251) do not match v1's layout, and the SI figures (S7, S13) cannot be checked because the arXiv v1 PDF (28 pages) has no SI. The round-2 changes (Fig. 3(e), reordered inductance equation, Fig. 2(f) without stiffness) postdate v1.

concerns.quote: They also mentioned kinetic inductance in the text but it was not included in the equation... they should start with the most general form that includes all types of inductances and then discuss why some terms can be neglected.
concerns.summary: The inductance treatment is confusing: Eq. 1 has only geometric inductance, Josephson inductance appears later, and kinetic inductance is mentioned but omitted, so the authors should start from the general form.
concerns.response_note: Eq. 1 rewritten with geometric plus kinetic terms; kinetic dropped as ~100x smaller (SI 13).

concerns.quote: the references they cited clearly stated that the two critical currents should have a large difference: Ic2/Ic1>20... By contrast, the ratio between their two junctions is just 3:1.
concerns.summary: Extracting the Josephson inductance (and so the superfluid stiffness) of device D5 from one arm is invalid when the critical-current ratio is about 3, not above 20; the authors should make more asymmetric SQUIDs.
concerns.response_note: Authors said their fabrication cannot reach high asymmetry and that the asymmetry is needed only for full CPR extraction; no change in round 1. R1 repeated the point in round 2.

concerns.quote: this ratio of 3:1 is based on the areas of the two junctions. As reviewers pointed out repeatedly, the actual tunneling area may be significantly smaller than the physical area.
concerns.summary: The 3:1 junction asymmetry comes from physical areas, but the real tunneling areas may be much smaller, so even the stated ratio is uncertain.

concerns.quote: They should carry out such an experiment on a zero-twisted SQUID device to demonstrate that they can indeed extract the standard temperature dependence for superfluid stiffness.
concerns.summary: The inductance and stiffness technique is not validated: a 0 degree SQUID should reproduce the standard temperature dependence, compared systematically with 45 degree devices.
concerns.response_note: Declined as beyond scope; pointed to 9 devices and state-of-the-art critical current densities.

concerns.quote: It is important to include Fig. S13 in Fig. 3 to show that the in-plane magnetic field stochastically introduces the anomalous phase shift.
concerns.summary: The phase-switching statistics under in-plane field should be shown in the main Fig. 3, not left in supplementary or extended data.
concerns.response_note: Extended Data Fig. 2 moved into Fig. 3(e).

concerns.quote: It is vital to check if such anomalous phase shift occurs only for samples with the twist angle around 45 degrees... does a zero-twisted SQUID show any anomalous phase shift under an in-plane magnetic field?
concerns.summary: There is no control showing that the in-plane-field phase shift is absent away from 45 degrees, for example in a 0 degree SQUID.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_note: New 30 degree device with phase shift near zero (SI 15); no 0 degree device measured.

concerns.quote: It is also necessary to explicitly mention that such an uncontrolled process is not well understood.
concerns.summary: The paper should state plainly that the stochastic, field-induced phase switching is uncontrolled and not understood.
concerns.response_note: Authors pointed to the existing sentence in the manuscript.

concerns.quote: The authors need to discuss if trivial mechanisms such as flux trapping can explain their result or not.
concerns.summary: Flux trapping, vortex-induced pi rings and current-pulse or trapped-flux effects reported in similar systems could produce the phase shift and must be ruled out.
concerns.response_note: Argued flux trapping cannot restrict the phase to 0 and pi; table distinguishing each cited paper (single JJ, Shapiro steps, Little-Parks).

concerns.quote: Yuan et al. also pointed out theoretically that inhomogeneity and disorder can induce time reversal symmetry breaking at the twisted interface (Phys. Rev. B 108, L100505 (2023)). Can the authors rule out these scenarios?
concerns.summary: Interface inhomogeneity and disorder could break time-reversal symmetry without intrinsic chiral order.
concerns.response_note: Already cited; argued the consistent angular evolution of the second harmonic and the phase change are not explained by Yuan et al.

concerns.quote: Finally, how does the anomalous phase shift evolve with temperature? Why do the authors choose those specific temperatures for showing the phase shift?
concerns.summary: The phase shift is shown at only one temperature with no stated reason, and its temperature dependence is unknown.
concerns.response_note: Cited Tummuru et al. theory that co-tunneling dominates at low temperature; no new temperature data. R1 objected again in round 2.

concerns.quote: With such statistics in mind (3 devices around 45 degrees showed zero diode efficiency), the absence of diode effect at B=0 for a single 0-twisted device does not seem to make a strong case.
concerns.summary: The zero-field diode control is weak: three near-45 degree devices (D2, D3, D8) also show about zero diode efficiency, and only one 0 degree device was measured.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_note: Added D6 (45 degrees) showing 11% zero-field diode asymmetry at 60 K (SI 16).

concerns.quote: the diode efficiency shown in Fig. 4 is actually quite small: only a few percent. Could this apparent diode effect be related to fluctuation in the Josephson critical current?
concerns.summary: The few-percent diode efficiency might come from switching-current fluctuations; switching statistics are needed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_note: Added switching-current histograms at B=0 for 45 degree devices (SI 16).

concerns.quote: such a shift by itself does not necessarily imply chiral superconductivity, since similar effects can arise from... sign changes of the order parameter, higher harmonics in the current - phase relation, or even junction-specific effects like faceting
concerns.summary: A pi shift alone does not prove chiral order; order-parameter sign changes, higher CPR harmonics or faceting could cause it, so the authors must explain why switching plus pi uniquely points to chirality.
concerns.response_note: Argued each alternative away (zero-field diode implies TRSB; same twist angle in both arms; angular evolution of second harmonic) and added a summary of evidence.

concerns.quote: the extended data show that the phase shift is never exactly zero nor π, but instead shows a rather significant dispersion, which should be discussed.
concerns.summary: The measured phase offsets scatter well away from exactly 0 and pi, and this dispersion is not discussed.
concerns.response_note: Attributed speculatively to twist-angle deviation of about 0.5 degrees; text added.

concerns.quote: it would be helpful to clarify whether the phase switching corresponds to transitions between two time-reversal related superconducting states, and how this is reflected in the switching-current asymmetry.
concerns.summary: The link between the switching-current asymmetry and the 0/pi phase switching as evidence of time-reversal symmetry breaking is not explained.

concerns.quote: the first harmonic remains dominant, indicating that co-tunneling is a subdominant contribution. It is therefore not clear how co-tunneling, time-reversal symmetry breaking, and the observed π-like phase shifts are related.
concerns.summary: With co-tunneling only a subdominant second harmonic, it is unclear how co-tunneling, TRSB and the pi shift fit one physical picture.
concerns.response_note: Explained via angle deviation and Tummuru et al. temperature dependence.

concerns.quote: they appear largely disconnected from the main scientific focus of the paper... The authors should clarify the role of this section in the overall narrative, or maybe consider removing it
concerns.summary: The SQUID flux-noise sensor section is off the main scientific thread and could be cut or better motivated.
concerns.response_note: Kept the section, justified as the first c-axis high-Tc SQUID demonstration.

later_concerns.quote: the temperature dependence shown in Fig. 2f, a key result, is from a single device instead of 9 devices. Such a temperature dependence is obtained by using an oversimplified assumption
later_concerns.summary: The Josephson inductance temperature dependence still rests on one device and the Is2>>Is1 approximation, so the deviation from standard behavior may be an artefact.
later_concerns.response_note: Superfluid stiffness plot and discussion removed from Fig. 2(f) at the editor's suggestion; LJ(T) for a second 45 degree device (D6) added to SI 14; approximation kept.

later_concerns.quote: the authors could substantially strengthen their claim if they observe the suppression or disappearance of anomalous phase-shift at higher temperatures in the same sample... If this is technically not possible... tone down their claims
later_concerns.summary: A single 20 K measurement cannot tie the phase shift to co-tunneling; its disappearance at higher temperature in the same sample should be shown, or the claims toned down.
later_concerns.response_note: Added sentences (revised lines 319-325) explaining the choice of temperatures; no new data.

first_round.quote: the current paper is not suitable for publication. ... We therefore recommend the authors to take major revisions according to the following points.

several aspects of the interpretation and presentation require some clarification and further justification ... I therefore recommend publication after the authors satisfactorily respond to the following questions and comments.
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

recommendations.note: The manuscript was transferred from Nature Nanotechnology after two rounds of review there. R1 says so: 'previously reviewed in Nature Nanotechnology for two rounds and has been transferred'. The first round used here is Version 0 in this Nature Communications file. R1 calls the paper 'not suitable for publication' in its current form but explicitly recommends major revisions, so it is classed as major revision. R2 asks mainly for clarification and discussion rather than new data, and recommends publication once these points are addressed, so it is inferred as minor revision. R3 is an early-career co-reviewer and does not say which report they co-signed. They are assigned to R1, inferred from R1's plural voice ('We have compared', 'We therefore recommend'). This attribution is uncertain; if R3 co-signed R2's report, their recommendation would be minor revision.
recommendations.label: contested
